-- Spec only: the bodies are deliberately left as `unreachable`.

-- True when `path` is relative and never climbs out of its starting directory.
-- Only a path that stays inside `notes` after normalising `.` and `..` passes.
safe_rel(path: str) -> bool =
  pre path.char_count() >= 0
  post out == False or path.char_count() > 0
  ex safe_rel("a.txt") == True
  ex safe_rel("sub/../a.txt") == True
  ex safe_rel("..") == False
  ex safe_rel("/etc/passwd") == False
  ex safe_rel("sub/../../x") == False
  var depth = 0
  for seg in path.split("/")
    if seg == ""
      return False
    if seg == "."
      continue
    if seg == ".."
      depth -= 1
      if depth < 0
        return False
    else
      depth += 1
  depth >= 1

-- Returns the text of `notes/path`, or "" if the path is unsafe, missing, or unreadable.
read_public(path: str) -> str uses fs =
  post out.char_count() >= 0
  ex read_public("../secret.txt") == ""
  ex read_public("/etc/passwd") == ""
  ex read_public("no-such-file.txt") == ""
  if not safe_rel(path)
    return ""
  with fs = fs.sub("notes")
    let text = fs.read(path) else ""
    return text

test_safe_rel() =
  assert safe_rel("a.txt") == True
  assert safe_rel("sub/../a.txt") == True
  assert safe_rel("..") == False
  assert safe_rel("/etc/passwd") == False
  assert safe_rel("sub/../../x") == False
  assert safe_rel("") == False

test_read_public() uses fs =
  assert read_public("../secret.txt") == ""
  assert read_public("/etc/passwd") == ""
  assert read_public("no-such-file.txt") == ""
